newsitem.title: UK: Shell Chemicals, BASF in Dutch JV.
newsitem.headline: Shell Chemicals, BASF in Dutch JV.

text.p: Shell Chemicals Europe Ltd said on Monday it had signed a joint venture agreement with German chemical group BASF AG to set up the BASELL manufacturing joint venture in the Netherlands.
Shell said construction of the chemicals plant, which will cost around 900 million marks and come on stream in the second quarter of 1999, was scheduled to begin in May.
The plant is expected to produce 250,000 tonnes of propylene oxide and 550,000 tonnes of styrene monomer per annum.
Propylene oxide and derivatives are used to make polyurethane foams, polyesters and solvents. Styrene monomer is used to make a wide range of polystyrenes and high performance resins.
Shell said the project had been notified formally to the EC Commission and to regional Dutch authorities for environmental approvals.
